_about: Every editorial judgement applied to the AI-financing research table lives here,
written by hand and committed, so that scripts/load-financing-deals.js only applies
and checks rather than guessing. A row with no entry in `rows` is reported and
skipped, never loaded on a default.
`check` echoes the row's entity_a and event_date. If the source table is re-generated
and the rows shift, the echo stops matching and the loader refuses rather than
applying row 12's judgement to row 13's deal.

one entity, several names: Microsoft/Microsoft Azure, Amazon/AWS, Alphabet Google/Google Cloud, OpenAI Global
LLC/OpenAI PBC, HUMAIN/HUMAIN (PIF-owned) and Lambda/Lambda Compute II LLC are each
one company under two labels. Splitting them would draw one company as two
disconnected nodes, which reads as a fact about the market rather than a data defect.
TSMC Arizona is NOT TSMC: The CHIPS award went to TSMC Arizona Corporation, a US subsidiary. The source's own
brief says subsidiary versus parent matters, and a $11.6bn US federal grant attached
to the Taiwanese parent would misdescribe both the money and the policy.
US Department of Commerce is NOT us_gove: The existing `us_government` entity covers export controls and policy generally.
The CHIPS grantor is a named agency, and the graph is more useful with the actual

minority equity investment -> convertibl: Row 11 only. Part 1 of the report says Microsoft's EUR 15m in Mistral converted
into equity at the next round, so it was a note at the time of the deal.
Recording it as 'investment' would overstate what Microsoft owned in Feb 2024.
cloud commitments -> offtake: A commitment to buy compute over years is an offtake agreement, not a chip order.
'chip_order' in migration 0007 covers hardware; the largest figures in this dataset
are cloud capacity purchases, and the $250bn Azure order is not an order for chips.
AI factory financing agreement -> invest: Rows 31 and 32. Brookfield's up-to-$9bn and Nvidia's $1bn are project equity in a
data-centre expansion, not lending — the report describes both as funding a build,
with no facility, rate or security named.
absent on purpose: No mapping exists for 'joint venture formation', 'AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP)
formation', 'joint venture for AI campus', 'compute financing platforms MoU',
'debt financing facility', 'senior secured term loan B', 'construction loan for
build-to-suit data center', 'investment-grade GPU financing facility',
'long-term cloud spend commitment', 'Series E equity investment' or 'AI/digital
infrastructure financing agreement'. Every row using them is rejected below, and
migration 0020 adds only the four event_kind values the accepted rows need.
Un-rejecting one of those rows requires a new migration AND a mapping here — which
is the point: the enum should not fill up with values no row uses.

_publisher_class_notes: What KIND of publisher each host is, independent of how confident anyone is
in the claim. `confidence_tier` bottoms out at 'news_derived', so a Reuters
wire story and a newsletter post land on the same value; this is what lets a
reader tell them apart without opening the link. See migration 0021.
The loader REFUSES a host that is not listed here rather than defaulting to
something plausible. A silent default would classify the next unvetted
domain as ordinary news, which is the whole failure this column prevents.
'aggregator' is a site republishing others' filings or reporting; 'newsletter'
is an individual's or small outlet's write-up. Both are weak publishers, and
they are weak in different ways worth keeping apart.

5.why: Amazon completing the $4bn it announced in September 2023 is the SAME $4bn. Loading it as a second event puts $8bn in the table for $4bn of money, and dedup_hash cannot catch it because the dates genuinely differ.

8.why: Held back in the first pass because its only source is tech-insider.org. Joshua ruled on 2026-08-30 that this project may cite aggregators of this kind. The URL was re-probed and returns 200 with no redirect, so the domain question and the dead-link question both clear. The citation records publisher_class = 'aggregator' and is_checked = FALSE so a $100bn figure cannot render as though it came from a filing.

17.why: coreweave.com slug is truncated mid-word ('...-and-blackstone-to-m') and returns 404. Reconstructing the full slug ('...-to-meet-surging-demand-for-generative-ai') also 404s. A $2.3bn facility may not be loaded against a link that does not resolve.

18.why: investors.coreweave.com slug is truncated ('...-led-by-Blackstone-a') and returns 403; the reconstructed Q4 press-release path 404s. Same rule as row 17.

19.reject: the row conflates two separate transactions
19.why: RECOVERY ATTEMPTED 2026-08-30, FAILED. The Bloomberg source's own headline is 'Blue Owl-Led Group Lands $600 Million Loan for CoreWeave Data Center' — the JV RECEIVED the loan; it did not pay CoreWeave $600m. The row is really two transactions welded into one edge: a Societe Generale-led construction loan TO the JV, and a lease FROM the JV to CoreWeave. Either can be modelled; neither can be modelled without silently dropping the other, and the $600m belongs only to the first. Sponsor-to-vehicle does not rescue it: Blue Owl did not lend the $600m either. Recoverable only by splitting the row in two, which is an editorial decision about the source table rather than a repair of it. Bloomberg's body is paywalled, so the lease terms are unavailable.

b.why: Reuters describes 'lenders including Macquarie Group and Industrial Development Funding', naming Macquarie first; rule (b) gives the named lead the key and records the rest as participants.

members.name: Industrial Development Funding
members.note: Named alongside Macquarie in the Reuters report; share undisclosed.

21.why: 'term-loan investors' is not an entity and names no member, so consortium rule (c) applies: a financing edge with an anonymous end is not a fact about anyone. Compounded by the sole source being ccir.io, a domain this site has not decided it may cite.

22.why: RECOVERY ATTEMPTED 2026-08-30, FAILED. The GlobeNewswire release was fetched and read. It settles that Microsoft is NOT the payer — 'Anchored by Microsoft's offtake' — but does not supply one: the money is '$2.10bn U.S. private placement' plus a '$1.55bn delayed draw term loan', and the release describes the lenders only as 'a broad group of global financial institutions, asset managers and insurance investors'. Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan are named, but as 'joint lead managers and arrangers', which is who structured it rather than who paid. So consortium rule (c) applies exactly as it does to row 21's 'term-loan investors': the paying side names nobody, and events.from_entity_id is NOT NULL. Recoverable the moment a source names a lender.

24.why: newsroom.equinix.com returns 200 but redirects to newsroom.equinix.com/404. Also needs an event_kind of 'joint_venture', which migration 0020 deliberately does not add until a loadable row requires it.

25.why: investor.nvidia.com slug ends in a bare hyphen ('...-Brookfield-Goldman-') and returns 403. The single largest figure in the dataset ($500bn) may not rest on a truncated link. Also needs 'vendor_financing', not yet in the enum.

26.why: ir.blackrock.com press-release path is truncated and returns 403. Also needs 'joint_venture'.

28.why: mgx.ae returns 200 but redirects to the site homepage — the article path is gone. Also needs 'joint_venture'.

29.why: Held back in the first pass because its only source is fwdstart.me. Loaded under Joshua's 2026-08-30 ruling; URL re-probed and returns 200 with no redirect. publisher_class = 'newsletter'.

30.why: Same fwdstart.me link as row 29, loaded under the same ruling. The researcher flags it 'alleged' rather than a confirmed loop, and that flag is carried through to loop_status unchanged. Migration 0021 adds the 'credit_facility' event_kind this row needs: 'up to $1.2bn' is a ceiling the borrower may not fully draw, not a loan that was made.

32.why: The row says a_to_b (NAVER pays Nvidia $1bn) while its own loop_description says 'Nvidia invests $1B and provides DSX platform and GPUs'. The row contradicts itself and the contradiction resolves inside the row, so it is corrected here rather than rejected. Rows 19 and 22 could not be resolved this way and are rejected.
